title: epoch-aliasing-in-burst-token-reconciliation-cascading-client-429s
text:
epoch-aliasing-in-burst-token-reconciliation-cascading-client-429s

description:
During a cross-environment policy migration (hosted -> dedicated/private) some tenants experienced sustained opaque 429s. The spike affected a small set of high-throughput customers and persisted for ~45 minutes before mitigation. This ticket captures the investigation, root cause, short-term mitigations, and the permanent fix that prevents epoch aliasing in burst token reconciliation across our router, quota DB, and KV cache layers.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a tenant with long-lived dedicated pool assignment and a custom burst window override via admin API
2) Trigger a policy migration job that moves the tenant from hosted routing to dedicated pool and writes a migration-id header
3) Send sustained request traffic that exercises continuous-batching and prefix-caching (simulate 500 concurrent streams with variable sequence lengths)
4) Observe router rejecting requests with 429s despite quota DB showing available burst tokens in some shards and zero in others

root_cause:
A race between the migration job and the router's burst-window reconciliation allowed two different epoch identifiers ("epoch aliasing") to exist for the same tenant. The router computes remaining_tokens by subtracting local in-flight usage from a cached burst window stamped with epoch A, while the quota DB had already advanced to epoch B after migration. Because the router saw a stale epoch, its compute produced negative remaining_tokens which triggered a conservative fallback to global throttling. The fallback path didn't include the migration-id mapping, so requests were rejected with opaque 429s. This was amplified for Dedicated and Private deployments where the reconciliation window TTLs and KV cache invalidation were longer than in Hosted, creating a prolonged outage window.

mitigation_and_workarounds:
Immediate: toggled router emergency flag to bypass epoch check and consult authoritative quota DB for affected tenants (rolled out to two regions) — stopped the 429 spike within 12 minutes of flip
Short-term: launched a targeted reconciliation sweep (one-off job) that backfilled missing epoch mappings and forced cache invalidation for tenants in migration in both Hosted and Dedicated clusters
Workaround for customers: recommended short-lived request rate reduction and advised that we would perform reconciliation; provided ticket updates and incident timeline
Communications: Escalation leads posted to oncall channel, created customer-facing status updates, and notified impacted customers via direct PMs

fix_summary:
1) Router: change reconciliation protocol to include migration-id in burst-window keys and add safe-merge logic when epoch mismatch detected (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6123)
2) Quota DB: emit backward-compatible epoch alias map for configurable TTL so short migrations don't create ephemeral breaks (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quota-db/pull/198)
3) KV Cache: reduce default cache TTL for burst-window entries during migration to 10s and add watch-based invalidation for migration events (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/cache/pull/77)
4) Add integration test harness that simulates migrations under load and asserts no 429 regressions (tests added to infra/integration/migration-load)
5) Release: included in runtime-1.22 with a console flag to enable migration-aware reconciliation

rollout_plan:
Canary: deploy router and cache changes to a single canary cluster with synthetic migration traffic, monitor 429/error-rate, latency, and CPU for 2 hours
Gradual: 25% -> 50% -> 100% region rollout over 24 hours if canary green
Dedicated/Private: coordinate with infra ops to schedule out-of-band KV cache invalidation in private customer clusters (ops runbook updated)
Fallback: if 429 or latency regressions observed, toggle router to authoritative-db fallback mode and roll back KV TTL change

tests_and_validation:
Unit: added tests for epoch alias lookups and safe-merge behavior
Integration: migration-load harness (500 concurrent streams) validates no 429s and consistent token accounting across router/quota-db/cache
Stress: 2-hour soak in canary with synthetic tenants mirroring customer throughput profiles
Post-release: dashboard alert added to Grafana to detect epoch divergence >1s between router cache and quota DB for any tenant

postmortem_lessons:
TTL heuristics that differ across deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated/Private) introduce subtle windows for transient state inconsistency — we need consistent migration semantics across all runtimes
Fallback paths must be topology-aware: conservative fallbacks that ignore migration metadata can create larger customer-impacting outages
Add observability: emit migration-id in request logs and expose epoch delta metrics so reconciliation drift is visible to SREs and engineers
Operational: create an oncall runbook for migration incidents including immediate toggles, reconciliation job steps, and customer communication templates

notes:
Coordination: Private deployments required an ops window because cache invalidation touches HSM-backed key rotation in some customers — early outreach prevented longer outages for two enterprise tenants
Follow-ups: ENG-42100 (better migration testing in CI), PM-1102 (customer comms template for rate incidents), DES-314 (console indicator for in-flight migrations)
Status: changes merged and rolled out to production; monitoring shows no recurrence in 30 days
